messages:
Ash: CI canary image publish on master is red after my Dockerfile tweak (small copy + new layer). Push fails with a 403 from registry. Anyone seen this pattern before? :eyes:

ci-bot: CI job: https://ci.redwood.ai/12345 (buildx canary)
Log excerpt:
```
#23 pushing manifest for registry.redwood.ai/canary:sha-abc123...
error: failed to push to registry: denied: requested access to the resource is denied
manifest upload failed: unexpected status: 403
```

Michael: Can you paste the full docker/buildx command and whether this used the remote builder or a local build-runner?

Ash: Command is `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 -t registry.redwood.ai/canary:$GIT_SHA --push .`
Runner: build-runner-7 (eu-west-1) using our remote buildx cluster. I also see intermittent `empty blob` messages in earlier lines: `failed to upload blob: unexpected status: 403`

Laura: Two quick checks: 1) try rerunning with `--no-cache` (or set BUILDX_CACHE=0) to rule out a corrupted cache layer, 2) confirm that the builder still has fresh registry creds (we rotated tokens this morning).

Ash: Rerunning now with `BUILDX_NO_CACHE=1` and `docker buildx prune --all --force` in the job prep. Triggering a rerun (job id 12346).

ci-bot: Rerun triggered: https://ci.redwood.ai/12346
Short log:
```
Pushing layer sha256:...
Uploaded chunk 4/4
Finalizing manifest...
error: manifest upload failed: unexpected status: 403
```

Michael: If no-cache didn't help, my hunch is auth/proxy. The 403 on manifest finalization often means the registry accepted blobs but rejected manifest because token scope is wrong or expired. Which credential set is the runner using?

Ash: Runner has `RO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` from secrets-mgr v2. I see a token timestamp of `2026-03-17T08:59:02Z` on the runner. Ops rotated tokens at 09:00. Maybe the runner cached an old token between jobs.

ops: Looking at proxy logs for build-runner-7. I see repeated 403s at 09:05 and a service message: `token validation failed: token issued before rotation cutoff`. Will flush cached creds on that runner and restart the builder service.

Laura: Good catch. If ops restarts the builder and it still fails, try reverting the Dockerfile change as a quick bisect to be 100% sure it isn't the layer content causing a registry policy to reject (rare but possible with certain media types).

Michael: I can revert the canary PR and run the canary build in a few minutes. Assigning to me. (reaction: :thumbsup:)

Michael: Reverted PR, triggered build 12347. Still failing with 403 during manifest finalize. So this rules out the Dockerfile tweak. Escalating to infra.

ops: I restarted build-runner-7 and cleared cached registry tokens. Triggering a clean builder run now. Will follow-up with proxy logs.

ops: Proxy trace shows the manifest request was rejected because the token scope didn't include `push:manifest` for multipart uploads — old tokens had a narrower scope. After clearing, new job used fresh token and authentication succeeded. New build 12348 passed the push stage and published image.

Ash: Awesome, thanks team. Root cause: token rotation + cached creds on one builder causing 403s. Follow-up action: add a post-rotation hook to flush builder credential caches and a CI health check that validates registry pushes after rotation. I'll open a tiny follow-up ticket.

Laura: Sounds good. If anyone sees similar flakes, please ping `#eng-infra` and include the runner id.

Michael: Filed infra#987: "flush builder creds on token rotation + CI canary push check" and linked the logs. Closing this thread.
